title: Best Dehumidifier for Office (2026): Quiet Picks for Calls
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for an Office
dek: Dry air shouldn’t come with a soundtrack. These office dehumidifiers stay quiet enough for a video call.
description: The best dehumidifier for an office in 2026 — quiet picks for private and open-plan workspaces, desk minis, and a high-capacity unit for basement offices.
intro: An **office dehumidifier** has a job the others in your home don’t: it has to stay quiet enough for a phone call. A basement unit that roars for 20 minutes an hour is fine when nobody’s down there. Put that same machine three feet from your desk during a video meeting and it becomes the loudest voice on the call.

So we judged every pick on noise first, then coverage and convenience — Wi-Fi to check the tank from your desk, and drain hoses so nobody on the team has to empty a bucket. We also included a high-capacity option for converted basement and garage offices, where dampness is a bigger problem than noise.
Whether you work from a spare bedroom, a cubicle or a shared office suite, there’s a pick here sized for your space and your ears.
topPicksLead: For most offices, the **Midea Cube 20** is the one to buy: Consumer Reports rates it the quietest dehumidifier it has evaluated, and it adds Wi-Fi control for checking humidity without leaving your chair.

products.name: Midea Cube 20-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD20S1QWT)
pros: Rated about 45 dB — quietest in Consumer Reports’ ratings
Wi-Fi app shows humidity and tank status
Tank in the base empties less often than its size suggests
Compact cube looks at home in a workspace
cons: Still a compressor, so not truly silent
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the rare compressor dehumidifier quiet enough to share a room with a meeting in progress. The app means you’re not getting up every hour to check on it.
products.performance: Consumer Reports rates it the quietest model it has evaluated, at about 45 dB. Midea specs it for up to 1,500 square feet, though at least one big retailer lists it at 500 — either way it comfortably handles a private office. If it’s for a bedroom office, see our [best quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) list for more low-noise options.

products.name: hOmeLabs 8-Pint Wi-Fi Dehumidifier (HME010091N)
cons: Low DOE capacity for damp spaces
products.whyWeLoveIt: In a shared space, the best dehumidifier is the one nobody notices — and nobody has to empty. Quiet operation plus a drain hose checks both boxes.
products.performance: hOmeLabs rates it at around 38 dB on its low setting, about the level of a soft conversation, and lists coverage up to 1,800 square feet. Its DOE capacity is modest, so it’s best for offices that are stuffy rather than truly damp. Run the hose to a sink or drain so it can work through the whole day unattended. More from the brand in our [best hOmeLabs dehumidifier](/best/best-homelabs-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint Dehumidifier (FHDD5034W1)
cons: Being replaced by the FHDD5034Y1 at some stores
products.whyWeLoveIt: In a finished basement or garage conversion, moisture matters more than noise. A 50-pint unit keeps a below-grade workspace in a healthy range without constant attention.
products.performance: It holds a damp basement office in the EPA’s recommended 30–50% range and can drain continuously through a workday. It’s louder than our other picks, so set it to low during calls or run it hard before and after hours. Some retailers now carry the near-identical FHDD5034Y1 successor; treat the two as interchangeable. See our [best dehumidifier for finished basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-finished-basement/) guide for more.

products.name: Pro Breeze PB-03 Mini Dehumidifier
pros: No compressor — under 35 dB by Pro Breeze’s rating
Small enough for a desk or credenza
Auto shutoff with a full-tank light
products.whyWeLoveIt: When you can’t have any compressor hum in the background, a thermoelectric mini is the answer. It does its job with barely a whisper.
products.performance: Pro Breeze rates it for about 2,200 cubic feet — roughly a 250-square-foot room — and under 35 dB. Thermoelectric units pull far less water than compressor models, so it suits a small private office that feels a little sticky, not a damp one. Compare it with siblings in our [best Pro Breeze dehumidifier](/best/best-pro-breeze-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: TABYIK DH-CS01 Mini Dehumidifier
pros: Tucks under a desk or onto a shelf
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a cubicle or a single desk that feels clammy, this is the least expensive fix — and nobody nearby will notice it’s running.
products.performance: Its roughly 28 dB rating puts it among the quietest dehumidifiers sold. Coverage tops out around 280 square feet, and its small tank needs emptying regularly in humid weather. Treat it as a desk-zone helper rather than a room solution. For other tiny options, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: A typical 50-pint compressor dehumidifier runs around 50–55 dB — above both office noise guidelines. That’s why we favored quiet-rated and thermoelectric models for workspaces where people talk.

We don’t lab-test, so we don’t claim our own decibel readings. We compared manufacturer noise ratings and Consumer Reports’ published results, DOE capacity, coverage and drainage options, and read owner reviews for comments about noise on calls, rattling and tank-full interruptions.
We weighted noise most heavily, then convenience features like Wi-Fi and drain hoses, then capacity matched to typical office sizes — from a single desk to a converted basement.

sections.heading: What to look for in an office dehumidifier

items.label: A low noise rating
items.text: Look for 45 dB or less if you take calls. A sleep or low mode helps.

items.label: Capacity sized for the space
items.text: 8–20 pints for a private office, 20–35 for a larger shared one. An undersized unit runs flat out — and louder — all day.

items.label: Continuous drainage for shared spaces
items.text: A drain hose removes the “whose turn is it to empty the tank?” problem.

items.label: Thermoelectric only for small areas
items.text: Compressor-free minis are nearly silent but cover only a few hundred square feet.

items.label: Smart controls
items.text: Wi-Fi lets you check humidity without leaving your desk. Our [best Wi-Fi dehumidifier](/best/best-wifi-dehumidifier/) guide compares apps.

sections.heading: Dehumidifiers for office spaces: placement and quiet tips

items: Place the unit across the room from your desk and microphone, not beside them.
Keep it a foot or more from walls so air flows freely — a starved fan runs louder.
Set it on a rubber mat or carpet to stop vibration from carrying through the floor.
Run it on high before your workday or over lunch, then drop to low during calls.
Clean the filter monthly; a clogged filter makes the fan work harder and noisier.

blocks.text: For more placement advice, see [where to place a dehumidifier](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Signs your office needs a dehumidifier

items: Papers curl or feel limp, and envelopes stick together.
The room smells musty when you open the door on Monday.
A hygrometer reads above 60% for days at a time.
Condensation forms on windows or a cold exterior wall.
Electronics, books or a printer seem to collect a damp film.

blocks.text: Any one of these is worth fixing. Long stretches above 60% humidity encourage mold and dust mites and can be hard on paper records and equipment. If the office is in a basement, also check for leaks and grading problems outside, since a dehumidifier handles moisture in the air but not water coming through the walls. Our guide on [when to use a dehumidifier](/guides/when-to-use-a-dehumidifier/) covers the warning signs in more detail.

The **Midea Cube 20** is the best office dehumidifier for most people — quiet enough for calls and easy to check from your phone. Choose the **hOmeLabs 8-Pint Wi-Fi** for a shared space, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034W1** for a damp basement or garage office, and the near-silent **Pro Breeze PB-03** or **TABYIK DH-CS01** for a single desk or small room.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for an office?
faqs.a: The Midea Cube 20 (MAD20S1QWT) for most offices. Consumer Reports rates it the quietest it has evaluated at about 45 dB, and it has Wi-Fi control. For a single desk, a thermoelectric mini like the Pro Breeze PB-03 is quieter still.

faqs.q: How loud can an office dehumidifier be?
faqs.a: ANSI/ASA S12.2-2019 recommends background noise of 40 dB or less in a private office and 45 dB in an open-plan office. Many 50-pint units run 50–55 dB, so look for a quiet-rated model.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for an office space?
faqs.a: An 8–20 pint unit covers most private offices. A shared office over about 1,500 square feet does better with 20–35 pints and a drain hose. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) has more detail.

faqs.q: Can I use a mini dehumidifier at my desk?
faqs.a: Yes, for a small area. Thermoelectric minis are nearly silent but only cover a few hundred square feet and remove water slowly. They suit a cubicle or small office, not an open floor.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier help in a basement office?
faqs.a: Yes. Basement and garage offices tend to run damp, and keeping humidity between 30% and 50% prevents mold and musty smells. A 50-pint unit on a drain hose handles the job without daily attention.

faqs.q: Can a dehumidifier protect office electronics and paper?
faqs.a: Yes. Keeping humidity between about 30% and 50% helps prevent curled paper, musty files and moisture-related corrosion on electronics, especially in basement or garage offices.
